title: arXiv AI papers — Friday, 23 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred ordering from technical relevance and author-reported evaluation breadth, not popularity; citation evidence is limited for papers announced only days ago.

sections.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a benchmark of 300 matched safe/unsafe task pairs across six domains to test whether tool-using agents act safely when critical facts are omitted and whether they retrieve and use those facts appropriately.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Core-AI/ML cross-list, matched-world design, six-domain scope, and ten-model evaluation; these are demonstrated-relevance signals, not popularity measures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper claims EpiSEM-Bench separates unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery; its ten-model study finds that resistance to omissions does not by itself ensure useful recovery.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that cost-conscious evaluation used fast variants for two model families and that results may not generalize to larger models in those families.

sections.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
sections.abstract: The authors propose selecting partial reasoning traces by directly optimizing the probability that at least one retained trace finishes correctly, balancing quality and diversity to reduce the cost of test-time scaling.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: AI/language cross-list, explicit pass@k selection objective, and comparisons on eight open-weight reasoning models establish methodological and empirical relevance to inference-time reasoning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ PKTP method models correlated rollout outcomes, approximates pass@k with a submodular objective, and uses greedy selection; they report gains over quality-only and diversity-only pruning baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The method estimates joint rollout success from partial-trace representations; the authors identify stronger representations of rollout correctness as a natural next step.

sections.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
sections.abstract: The authors propose a training-free metric that measures alignment between sensory representations and physical motion, reporting positive correlations with downstream robot task success across embodied-model families.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-category CV/ML/robotics cross-list and evaluation across VLAs, VLMs, world-action models, and real-robot policies provide broad evidence for the proposed offline capability proxy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper claims Sensorimotor Alignment (S²) can help prioritize embodied models before expensive closed-loop evaluation and can explain selected representation-level behaviors.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors emphasize that the relationship with success is correlational; they also report limited model families, benchmarks, few models per comparison, and one real-robot setting.

sections.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
sections.abstract: METTA combines causal neural memory for within-episode adaptation with compact episode summaries for longer-range task inference, and the authors report results on held-out Meta-World tasks and sparse-reward PointMaze.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: AI/ML cross-list, held-out task-family evaluation, and comparison with transformer baselines on long-context tasks make this a relevant test-time adaptation result.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a two-timescale memory and test-time adaptation design intended to retain useful history with linear sequence complexity rather than attending over the full trajectory.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors frame experiments around fixed-task trials and identify continual or nonstationary settings, where temporal or recency information may matter, as future work.

sections.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
sections.abstract: This survey organizes video understanding, generation, unified models, and video world models as reading, writing, sharing, and interacting with latent evolving worlds, emphasizing persistent state and interaction-grounded evaluation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The 102-page survey synthesizes models, datasets, and benchmarks across four connected video-modeling paradigms; its value here is as a field-mapping reference, not a new experimental result.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a world-modeling lens and identify a shift from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllability, physical and causal validity, and downstream decisions.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a literature synthesis rather than an experimental validation of the proposed taxonomy; the paper cautions that strong performance on individual video tasks does not by itself establish general world-model capability.
